answer: One concrete defense is sediment-graded trust. A new identity starts at the base earning tiny jobs, and standing builds slowly, layer on layer like shale: only verified completions compact into the next tier. Access to larger contracts sits on a higher ledge held by old, attested identities, so a mass of fresh sybils can never bid for valuable work at once. Any sudden delta, one account jumping in output or value far past its layer, triggers peer re-verification before it advances. Attackers then face months of cheap labor per identity, which wrecks the economics of spinning up thousands.
